body: `inject_ready_cloud_catalog` first writes `cloud_models` into `_meta.wta`, but this second `inject_wta_meta` call replaces that entire namespace rather than merging it. Because the new identity metadata is now injected unconditionally, every initialize response with a ready host cloud catalog loses the catalog before reaching the helper, breaking the model picker for those agents. Build one trusted `WtaMeta` containing the catalog, resolved identity, and proposal capability, then inject it once.

The search stops at the first matching id/category before checking its kind. If an agent advertises a same-named non-Select entry before the valid Select entry, capability discovery incorrectly fails instead of continuing to the valid selector. Include the kind check in the predicate, as the model-selector path does.

The `{Locked}` annotation includes `/yolo`, but `/yolo` does not occur in this resource value. Locked-token comments are consumed as translator constraints and must name tokens actually present; remove `/yolo` from the annotation (the command name is rendered separately).

These live Copilot tests treat an installed but unauthenticated CLI as ready, then fail at `Wait-AgentReady` even though authentication is an external prerequisite. Determine readiness with `Get-AgentCliStatus` (retaining a separate installed-only flag if desired for the settings round-trip case) so unauthenticated environments are reported as skips rather than product failures.

body: The mapped C292 contract says policy overrides a stored global-on default and rejects `/yolo on`, but this test asserts only the slash-command rejection. It would still pass if startup incorrectly enabled provider-native Yolo despite the policy. Assert the initial session is reconciled off (or that no native-on operation occurs) before checking the command.

The lazy-session operation can apply a stale enable after a settings/GPO update. If `agent_config_changed` was queued before `SessionAttached` but is handled while this awaited RPC is in flight, the App sees no bound session and schedules no replacement operation; this task then completes the old enable and proceeds to the prompt even though the shared effective state is now off. Re-read the effective state after the RPC and synchronously apply any changed desired value (failing closed on disable failure) before allowing the first prompt.

Passing the broad `Software\Policies\Microsoft` key means this recursive watcher fires for policy changes belonging to every Microsoft product, causing unnecessary full settings reloads. Pass `PolicyRegKey` instead; `CreatePolicyChangeWatcher` already falls back to the deepest existing ancestor when the product key does not exist.
